### Toplines

LAST UPDATED: 11/13/26, 3:00pm ET

#### U.S. Congress

- **Women in the 120th Congress:  At least 160 women will serve in the 120th Congress in 2027, including 144 (120D, 24R) women who have already won their elections and 16 (13D, 3R) Senate holdovers. This will be a new record. (current record: 152, first set in 2024).  They will be at least 29.9% of all members of Congress. Currently, 152 (111D, 41R) women serve in the U.S. Congress, holding 28.4% of all seats. **Five (4D, 1R) women remain in congressional contests that are too close to call and 2 (2D) have advanced to a runoff election.  
- Women in the U.S. Senate: At least 23 (16D, 7R) women will serve in the U.S. Senate**  in 2027 **(current record: 27, set in 2026). They will be at least 23% of all members of the Senate. Currently, 27 (16D, 11R) serve in the U.S. Senate, holding 27% of all seats. One (1D) woman remains in a U.S. Senate contest that is too close to call, ensuring that  women’s representation in the U.S. Senate will drop from 2026 to 2027.  Three (3R) women Senate incumbents were defeated in the general election. 
- **Women in the U.S. House:  At least  137 women will serve in the U.S. House in 2027. This will be a new record (current record: 127, set in 2024). They will be at least 31.5% of all members of the U.S. House. Currently, 125 (95D, 30R) women serve in the U.S. House, holding 28.7% of all seats. **Four (3D, 1R) women remain in U.S. House contests that are too close to call and 2 (2D) have advanced to a runoff election.   Six (6R) women House incumbents were defeated in the general election. 

#### Statewide Elective Executive Office

- Women Governors: At least 18 (15D, 3R) women will serve as governors in 2027. They will be at least 36% of all governors in the U.S. Currently, 14 (10D, 4R) women serve as governor, holding 28% of all seats. One (1R) woman remains in a gubernatorial contest that is too close to call in Alaska.  No incumbent women governors were defeated in the general election. 
- **Women in Statewide Elective Executive Office (including governor):  At least 108 (75D, 32R, 1NP) women will serve in statewide elective executive office (including governor)  in 2027. They will be at least 34.7% of all statewide elective executive officials. Currently, 98 (55D, 42R, 1NP) women serve in statewide elective executive offices, holding 31.6% of these positions. **Three (1D, 2R) women remain in four statewide executive contests that are too close to call.  Four (4R) women incumbents holding statewide elective executive office were defeated in the general election.

#### Milestones

*Numerous milestones were set for women’s representation in 2026. What follows is a selection of national and state milestones. *

##### National Milestones

- Keisha Lance Bottoms (D-GA) will be the first Black American woman to serve as governor in the United States.
- Deb Haaland (D-NM) will be the first Native American woman to serve as governor in the United States.
- Peggy Flanagan (D-MN) will be the first Native American woman to serve in the U.S. Senate.
- A record three Black women will serve concurrently in the U.S. Senate for the first time in 2027: Senators Angela Alsobrooks (D-MD) and Lisa Blunt Rochester (D-DE) and Juliana Stratton (D-IL).
- Illinois will be the first state to be represented by two women of color senators simultaneously: Senator Tammy Duckworth (D) and Juliana Stratton (D).
- New Mexico is the first state to elect an all women of color gubernatorial ticket: governor-elect Deb Haaland (D) and lieutenant governor-elect Stephanie Garcia Richard (D). 
- In 2027, women will serve concurrently as governor and lieutenant governor in nine states: Arkansas, Massachusetts, Michigan, New Jersey, New Mexico, New York, Rhode Island, Texas, and Virginia. Women were elected on the same general election gubernatorial ticket this year in Massachusetts, Michigan, New Mexico, and New York. 

##### State Milestones

- This year, four states elected their first woman governor: Georgia, Minnesota, Ohio, and Tennessee. While no woman previously served as governor in Georgia, Minnesota, or Tennessee, a woman briefly held the governorship in Ohio through succession. Fourteen states remain that have never had a woman governor. Amy Acton (D) is the first woman  elected governor of Ohio. Nancy Hollister (R) served briefly as governor via succession in 1998-1999. Marsha Blackburn (R-TN) will be the first woman to serve as governor of Tennessee. Keisha Lance Bottoms (D-GA) will be the first woman to serve as governor of Georgia. Amy Klobuchar (D-MN) will be the first woman to serve as governor of Minnesota.
- Adrienne Adams (D) will be the first Black woman to be elected as lieutenant governor in New York.
- Annie Andrews (D) is the first woman *elected *to the U.S. Senate from South Carolina and will be the first Democratic woman to serve in the U.S. Senate from South Carolina.
- Teresa Benitez-Thompson (D-02) will be the first Latina to serve in the U.S. House from Nevada.
- Jena Griswold (D) will be the first Democratic woman to serve as attorney general in Colorado.
- Amanda Gonzalez (D-Secretary of State) will be the first Latina to serve in statewide elective executive office in Colorado.
- Gina Hinojosa (D) will be the first Latina to serve as governor of Texas.
- Melat Kiros (D-01) will be the first Black woman to serve in Congress from Colorado.
- Julia Letlow (R) will be the first Republican woman to serve in the U.S. Senate from Louisiana.
- Tya Mathis-Coleman (D-Treasurer) will be the first Black woman to serve in statewide elective executive office in Nevada.
- Denise Powell (D-02) will be the first Latina to serve in Congress from Nebraska and the first Democratic woman to serve in the U.S. House from Nebraska.
- Claire Valdez (D-07) will be the first Native American woman to serve in Congress from New York.
- JoCasta Zamparripa (D-Secretary of State) will be the first Latina to serve in statewide elected executive office in Wisconsin.
- Black women will hold 9 of 13 (69.2%) statewide elective executive offices in Georgia in 2027. 
- Clara Pratte (D-Corporation Commission) will be the first Native American woman to serve in statewide elective executive office in Arizona.
 

### U.S. Senate

In 2026, 7 (3D, 4R) women won contests for the U.S. Senate. When combined with the 16 (13D, 3R) incumbent women senators not up for election this year, at least 23 (16D, 7R) women will serve in the Senate in the 120th Congress. As of Election Day 2026, 27 (16D, 11R) women serve in the U.S. Senate. One (1D) woman remains in a U.S. Senate contest that is too close to call, ensuring that women’s representation in the U.S. Senate will drop from 2026 to 2027. 

Of the 7 (3D, 4R) women winners of U.S. Senate contests in 2026:

- 2 (2R) are incumbents; 
- 4 (2D, 2R) won open seats; and
- 1 (1R) defeated an incumbent.  

In total, 9 (3D, 6R) women Senate incumbents will depart office at the end of 2026, including:

- Three (3R) women Senate incumbents - Senators Susan Collins (R-ME), Darline Graham (D-SC), and Cindy Hyde Smith (R-MS) who were defeated in the general election; 
- Four (2D, 2R) women Senate incumbents who did not seek re-election; and
- Two (1D, 1R) more women incumbents who successfully ran for governor this year. 

Follow this link for a complete and sortable list of women who will serve in the 120th Congress in 2027.

Breakdowns by officeholder race/ethnicity are below, indicating the following milestones:

- For the first time, a Native American woman (Peggy Flanagan, D-MN) will serve in the U.S. Senate. 
- A record three Black women will serve concurrently in the U.S. Senate for the first time in 2027: Angela Alsobrooks (D-MD), Lisa Blunt Rochester (D-DE), and Juliana Stratton (D-IL).
- Illinois will be the first state to be represented by two women of color senators simultaneously: Tammy Duckworth (D) and Juliana Stratton (D). 

The U.S. Senate will continue to have zero MENA women members. No MENA women have ever served in the U.S. Senate. 

Additional state-based milestones among women who have won U.S. Senate contests in 2026 include:

- Julia Letlow (R) will be the first Republican woman to serve in the U.S. Senate from Louisiana and the first woman to serve since 2015.
- Annie Andrews (D) is the first woman *elected *to the U.S. Senate from South Carolina and will be the first Democratic woman to serve in the U.S. Senate from South Carolina.

### U.S. House

At least**  137 women will serve in the U.S. House in 2027. This will be a new record (current record: 127, set in 2024). They will be at least 31.5% of all members of the U.S. House. Currently, 125 (95D, 30R) women serve in the U.S. House, holding 28.7% of all seats. **Four (3D, 1R) women remain in U.S. House contests that are too close to call and 2 (2D) have advanced to a runoff election.  

A record number of women overall and Democratic women will serve in the U.S. House in 2027.

In addition, 4 (2D, 2R) non-voting delegates from American Samoa, Guam, the Northern Mariana Islands, and the U.S. Virgin Islands will serve in the 120th Congress. Four (2D, 2R) women serve as non-voting delegates as of Election Day 2026. Non-voting delegates are not included in counts and records reported here. 

Of the 137 (117D, 20R) women winners of U.S. House contests in 2026:

- 100 (83D, 17R) are incumbents;
- 22 (19D, 3R) won open seats; and
- 15 (15D) defeated incumbents.

Thirty-seven (34D, 3R) non-incumbent women won contests for the U.S. House in 2026. Another 3 (3D) non-incumbent women are in U.S. House contests that are too close to call, and 2 (2D) have advanced to a runoff. The number of non-incumbent women House winners in 2027 surpass the current record 36 new House women in a single election, set in 2018. The current record for non-incumbent Democratic women winners of U.S. House seats in a single election is 35, set in 2018. The current record for non-incumbent Republican women winners of U.S. House seats in a single election is 19, set in 2020.

In total, 24 (12D, 12R) women House incumbents will depart office at the end of 2026, including:

- 7 (7R) women House incumbents were defeated in the general election; 
- 15 (10D, 5R) women House incumbents who did not seek re-election; and 
- 2 (2D) women incumbents were defeated in primary elections. 

Follow this link for a complete and sortable list of women who will serve in the 120th Congress in 2027.

Breakdowns by officeholder race/ethnicity are below, indicating that no new highs have yet been achieved for U.S. House representation within any race/ethnic group. With some races still to be called, however, Latinas have reached a new record for U.S. House and congressional representation, Black women have reached a new record for congressional representation, and both Middle Eastern/North African and Native American/Alaska Native/Native Hawaiian women have matched the current record for representation in the U.S. House.

Additional state-based milestones among women who have won U.S. House contests in 2026 include:

- Teresa Benitez-Thompson (D-02) will be the first Latina to serve in the U.S. House from Nevada.
- Melat Kiros (D-01) will be the first Black woman to serve in Congress from Colorado.
- Denise Powell (D-02) will be the first Latina to serve in Congress from Nebraska and the first Democratic woman to serve in the U.S. House from Nebraska.
- Claire Valdez (D-07) will be the first Native American woman to serve in Congress from New York.

### Governor

In 2026, 16 (13D, 3R) women won gubernatorial contests. When combined with 2 (2D) incumbent women governors not up for re-election this year, at least 18 (15D, 3R) women will serve as governors in 2027. They will be 36% of all governors in the U.S. This will be a new record high for women governors overall and Democratic women governors. One (1R) woman remains in a gubernatorial contest that is too close to call in Alaska. 

Of the 16 (13D, 3R)  women winners of gubernatorial contests in 2026:

- 6 (4D, 2R) are incumbents;
- 9 (8D, 1R) won open seats; and
- 1 (1D) defeated an incumbent.

No incumbent women governors were defeated in the general election. Six (4D, 2R) women House incumbents did not seek re-election due to term limits or retirement.

Breakdowns by officeholder race/ethnicity are below, indicating notable firsts in gubernatorial representation:

- Keisha Lance Bottoms (D-GA) will be the first Black woman to serve as governor in the United States and the first woman to serve as governor of Georgia.
- Deb Haaland (D-NM) will be the first Native American woman to serve as governor in the United States.

No MENA women have ever served as governor in the U.S. 

Additional state-based milestones among women who have won gubernatorial contests in 2026, including:

- Amy Acton (D) is the first woman  elected governor of Ohio; the first and only woman governor of Ohio – Nancy Hollister (R) – served briefly as governor from December 31, 1998 to January 11, 1999 via succession due to the resignation of the incumbent governor.
- Marsha Blackburn (R-TN) will be the first woman to serve as governor of Tennessee.
- Gina Hinojosa (D) will be the first Latina to serve as governor of Texas.
- Amy Klobuchar (D-MN) will be the first woman to serve as governor of Minnesota.

When these new women governors enter office in 2027, fourteen states will remain that have never had a woman governor.

Three U.S. territories also held gubernatorial elections in 2026: Guam, the Northern Mariana Islands, and the U.S. Virgin Islands. Current U.S. Delegate Stacey Plaskett was successful in her bid to become Governor of the U.S. Virgin Islands. Currently, two women serve among the five territorial governors: Jenniffer González-Colón (Puerto Rico) and Lou Leon Guerrero (Guam). Guerrero was term-limited in 2026.  

### Statewide Elective Executive Office

In 2026, 80 (62D, 17R, 1NP) women won statewide elective executive offices, including governor. They will join the 28 (13D, 15R) women currently serving as statewide elective executive officials who were not up for re-election this year. Combined, at least 108 (75D, 32R, 1NP) women will serve in statewide elective executive office, including governor, in 2027. They will be at least 34.6% of all statewide elected executive officeholders in the U.S. As of Election Day 2026, 97 (54D, 42R, 1NP) women served in statewide elective executive office. Three (1D, 2R) women remain in nine statewide executive contests that are too close to call. 

Of the 80 (62D, 17R, 1NP) women winners statewide executive contests in 2026:

- 32 (22D, 9R, 1NP) are incumbents; 
- 38 (30D, 8R) won open seats; and
- 10 (10D) defeated incumbents.

Four (4R) women incumbents holding statewide elective executive offices were defeated in the general election. In addition, 34 (20D, 14R) are departing their current office due to retirement, term limits, running for other offices, or primary defeat. 

Follow this link for a complete and sortable list of women who will serve in statewide elective executive office (including governor) in 2027.

Breakdowns by officeholder race/ethnicity are below, indicating that Black women and Latinas will reach a new high for statewide elective executive representation in 2027.

In 2027, women will serve concurrently as governor and lieutenant governor in nine states: Arkansas, Massachusetts, Michigan, New Jersey, New Mexico, New York, Rhode Island, Texas, and Virginia. Women were elected on the same general election gubernatorial ticket this year in Massachusetts, Michigan, New Mexico, and New York. New Mexico is the first state to elect an all women of color gubernatorial ticket: governor-elect Deb Haaland (D) and lieutenant governor-elect Stephanie Garcia Richard (D). 

Additional state-based milestones among women who have won statewide executive contests other than governor in 2026 include:

- Adrienne Adams (D) will be the first Black woman to be elected as lieutenant governor in New York.
- Jena Griswold (D) will be the first Democratic woman to serve as attorney general in Colorado.
- Amanda Gonzalez (D-Secretary of State) will be the first Latina to serve in statewide elective executive office in Colorado.
- Tya Mathis-Coleman (D-Treasurer) will be the first Black woman to serve in statewide elective executive office in Nevada.
- JoCasta Zamparripa (D-Secretary of State) will be the first Latina to serve in statewide elective executive office in Wisconsin.
- Black women will hold 9 of 13 (69.2%) statewide elective executive offices in Georgia in 2027. 
- Clara Pratte (D-Corporation Commission) will be the first Native American woman to serve in statewide elective executive office in Arizona.

Flames, NHL, Fanatics Unveil Hometown Remix Jersey, Apparel, Headwear Collection | Calgary Flames

# Flames, NHL, Fanatics Unveil Hometown Remix Jersey, Apparel, Headwear Collection 

 Flames set to wear Hometown Remix jersey nine times 

By Calgary Flames Staff

 CalgaryFlames.com 

 November 02, 2026 

Today, the Calgary Flames, NHL and Fanatics unveiled the club’s Hometown Remix uniform, a special edition look that celebrates the fans, fabric, culture of Calgary and the Scotiabank Saddledome. Part of a league-wide program featuring all 32 clubs, the Calgary Flames uniform was designed in collaboration with Fanatics, the League’s on-ice uniform provider, and the NHL and marks the culmination of a two-year development process. 

The Calgary Flames will wear their hometown remix uniforms nine times during the 2026-27 season, beginning on Friday, November 6th, 2026, when they host the Anaheim Ducks at Scotiabank Saddledome.

The Calgary Flames will wear their Hometown Remix uniforms on the following dates, all of which will take place at the Scotiabank Saddledome.

• Friday, November 6th, 2026, vs. Anaheim Ducks

• Sunday, November 8th, 2026, vs. Philadelphia Flyers

• Wednesday, November 11th, 2026, vs. New York Rangers

• Thursday, December 3rd, 2026, vs. Buffalo Sabres

• Saturday, December 5th, 2026, vs. Washington Capitals

• Tuesday, December 8th, 2026, vs. Nashville Predators

• Tuesday, January 12th, 2027, vs. Columbus Blue Jackets

• Thursday, January 14th, 2027, vs. San Jose Sharks

• Saturday, January 16th, 2027, vs. Los Angeles Kings

The Hometown Remix jersey is the perfect fit for the Scotiabank Saddledome Farewell Season

#### Hometown Remix Jersey

Talk about some sweet new threads!

Each Hometown Remix uniform was designed around its respective city and fanbase. Design details throughout the collection draw on local landmarks, motifs and culture, grounding each look in something recognizable to fans. There is nothing more recognizable in Calgary than the home of the Calgary Flames, the Scotiabank Saddledome.

> In the wise words of Matt Coronato: WOW 😍 pic.twitter.com/NKekUgzdcw
> 
> — Calgary Flames (@NHLFlames) November 2, 2026

Hometown Remix jerseys celebrate the people and places that make each city so great. And nowhere is this more poignant than Calgary, celebrating the last year of Flames in the Saddledome. Housing every home game since 1983, this arena has seen it all. Worthy opponents. Dramatic battles. Floods! It’s become more than a building. It’s an anchor for community. A physical legacy. One that will live on in your Hometown Remix jersey. From the signature texture of the arena ceiling on the “88 Gold” front crest, to the iconic window shape debossed into the sleeve striping and the arena roofline reflected in the exterior hem striping, no detail has been spared. On the hem, you’ll also find the year the Saddledome was opened, along with the year it will close, ending an important and storied chapter of the Flames. Even the custom block numbers feature the texture of the shutters. Celebrate for one more year, showing up to home games in your Hometown Remix jersey and honour the impact this iconic arena has had on the city.

“There are few things as identifiable with Calgary and the Calgary Flames as the Scotiabank Saddledome.” said Robert Hayes, President and Chief Executive Officer of Calgary Sports & Entertainment Corporation. “For our Farewell Season, we are proud to have partnered with the NHL and Fanatics to create a uniform that pays tribute to the building that has been part of the fabric of this city since 1983. The Hometown Remix uniform provides an incredible opportunity for our fans to take a piece of the Scotiabank Saddledome with them long after this season is over and celebrate the memories made under its iconic roof for years to come.”

“Few symbols in sports carry the history, pride, and emotional connection of an NHL sweater,” said Brian Jennings, NHL Senior Executive Vice President and Chief Partnerships and Club Strategy Officer. “Hometown Remix builds on that legacy in a fresh and authentic way, celebrating the fans, culture and communities that make each NHL market unique. Together with Fanatics and our Clubs, we’ve created designs that are rooted in local identity and tell a story about the cities and fans they represent. We’re incredibly excited to bring the program to life and see that passion reflected both on the ice and in the stands.”

“Hometown Remix represents the most exciting initiative our team has designed and delivered with our partners since we hit the ice with the NHL in 2024,” said Dom Fillion, Vice President of Creative Design for Fanatics. “What makes this program so special is the collaboration with each club and together leaning into the history, culture, fabric and identity of every city and fan base to make sure these felt as authentic and personal as possible. We can’t wait to see them worn by the teams on the ice and the fans in the stands all season long.”

Hometown Remix jerseys – both the on-ice Authentic Pro and Premium versions - and a cutting-edge assortment of headwear and men's and women's fan gear, including hoodies, tees and brand new fleece and outerwear styles, are available beginning today across the Fanatics network of sites, including NHLShop.com, NHLShop.ca and Fanatics.com, as well as team stores and the NHL Shop NYC flagship store.

case.old_text: One consequence of the tension between Yugoslavia and the Soviet Union was Tito's decision to begin large-scale repression against enemies of the government. This repression was not limited to known and alleged Stalinists, but included members of the Communist Party, or anyone exhibiting sympathy towards the Soviet Union. Prominent partisans, such as Vlado Dapčević, were victims of this repression, which lasted until 1956 and was marked by violations of human rights. Tens of thousands of political opponents served in forced labour camps, such as Goli Otok (Barren Island), and hundreds died. A disputed, but feasible number, put forth by the Yugoslav government in 1964, places the number of Goli Otok inmates incarcerated between 1948 and 1956 to be 16,554, with fewer than 600 having died during detention. The facilities at Goli Otok were abandoned in 1956, and jurisdiction of the now-defunct political prison was handed over to the government of the Socialist Republic of Croatia.

case.old_text: Victor Frankenstein, whose character name has sometimes evolved in popular culture to Dr. Frankenstein, is a fictional character who first appeared as the titular main protagonist of Mary Shelley's 1818 novel Frankenstein; or, The Modern Prometheus. He is a young Italian-born Swiss scientist who, after studying chemical processes and the decay of living things at university, gains an insight into the creation of life and gives life to his own creature (often referred to as Frankenstein's monster, or often colloquially referred to as simply "Frankenstein"). Victor later regrets meddling with nature through his creation, as he inadvertently endangers his own life and the lives of his family and friends when the creature seeks revenge against him. He is first introduced in the novel when he is seeking to catch the monster near the North Pole and is saved from potential fatality by Robert Walton and his crew.

case.old_text: Next Generation gave the Saturn version of the game three stars out of five, commending the gameplay despite faulting some elements in the game design. GamePro said that "Head-to-head games, tournament options, penalty shootouts, awesome cinematics, instant replays, and more score a goal for Victory." Games World rated the game 65% and stated that even though it substituted international teams for Japanese teams, "the UK game still struggles to score". Ultimate Future Games rated the game 70% and said that it "just doesn't have the depth or ease of play of its contemporaries" while praising its angles and views. MAXIMUM Magazine gave the game two stars and called it "a frankly unacceptable release" noting that is visuals did not make up for its poor gameplay.

Ultimate Future Games rated the game 70% and said that it "just doesn't have the depth or ease of play of its contemporaries" while praising its angles and views. MAXIMUM Magazine gave the game two stars and called it "a frankly unacceptable release" noting that is visuals did not make up for its poor gameplay. The original Japanese Victory Goal received a score of 78% from Australian magazine Hyper in June 1995. Reviewer Ben Mansill praised its attractive graphics, rotating camera perspectives and multiplayer gameplay, but criticised the simplistic controls, artificial intelligence and background music. Although he regarded the game as enjoyable with other players, he considered its single-player experience less sophisticated than FIFA International Soccer.

case.old_text: The Welsh Rebellion of 1211 was a rebellion by several Welsh princes, orchestrated by Llywelyn ab Iorwerth with primary support from Gwenwynwyn ab Owain Cyfeiliog, Maelgwn ap Rhys, and Madog ap Gruffudd Maelor, against King John of England.  Although technically defeated, this uprising resulted in increased independence from England for the Welsh.

# Troy’s Treasures: Troy native with a glorious voice 

By Troy Record | troyrecord@medianewsgroup.com

PUBLISHED: December 11, 2011 at 1:25 PM EST | UPDATED: July 21, 2021 at 10:36 AM EDT

One of the most beautiful of all Christmas hymns is “O Holy Night” composed in 1847 by Adolphe Adam, a prolific artist best known for composing the ballets “Giselle” and “La Corsaire.” The lyrics were based on a French poem by Placide Cappeau and edited by John Sullivan Dwight, a Unitarian minister and author of “Dwight’s Journal of Music.” Countless times over the years, choir members of all ages have sung the hymn in school Christmas pageants and at church services. Little did a young choir member at St. Anthony of Padua Shrine Church in Troy know at the time that singing this hymn would later be her launching pad for a popular, steady and accomplished vocal career which spanned the 1940s to the 1970s. Olivia Bonelli, the daughter of Louis and Jenny Riccardi Bonelli, was born on July 2, 1920, the eldest of six children including brothers Louis A. and Peter and sisters, Terese, Jane and Mary. Louis Sr. was an accomplished local stone mason and his expert brownstone work, later continued by his son Louis A., can still be seen on the facades of many of Troy’s elegant brownstones. The family were longtime resident of 1454 Seventh Ave. adjacent to Prospect Park south of Ferry Street. Like her siblings, Olivia attended St. Anthony’s School then located in the former Public School 8 at 1471 Fifth Ave. a few blocks from her home. Possessor of a gifted voice and encouraged by her family, Olivia began voice studies with Charles Pickering, who taught at Emma Willard, the prestigious girls preparatory school on Pawling Avenue, and gave her first recital at the school’s concert hall. In 1945 after Olivia successfully auditioned for the chorus of Radio City Music Hall, she stepped in at the last minute to sing “O Holy Night” at the hall’s famed Christmas Show, a song familiar to the young Troy woman — except this time she would be singing for the first time accompanied by a full symphony orchestra! The film that preceded the stage production was Leo McCarey’s now classic holiday film “The Bells of St. Mary’s” staring Bing Crosby and Ingrid Bergman. As a result of this solo, Olivia went on to become a featured performer with the company appearing for more than three years in all of the Music Hall’s major stage productions. The Troy native soprano can also claim to be one of the early pioneers in live televised opera, which opened the venue to millions via the airwaves appearing in an ABC-TV production of LaTrivata in 1959. In 1967, she appeared with the Metropolitan Opera for a first reading of American composer Marvin David Levy’s opera based on Eugene O’Neill’s play “Mourning Becomes Electra.” Early in her career she toured with the Starlighters, a USO group that sang for wounded service members in hospitals throughout the country. Her most requested solos on the tour were Gounod’s “Ave Maria” and Victor Herbert’s “Italian Street Song.” Peter Bonelli tells us that despite the grueling schedule she had the rest of her life, entertaining wounded service members was the most meaningful experience of his sister’s life. Olivia performed with the New York City Opera and major opera companies across America. Her beautiful, clear expressive soprano voice was heard by thousands of opera fans throughout America in roles from Mimi in La Boheme to Gilda in Rigoletto to Michaela in Carmen. She returned to Troy in the 1950s for a performance at the Troy Savings Bank Music Hall after her success in New York. In the early 1950s she married George Ortell, a performing tenor who then went on to establish a successful greeting card enterprise. Olivia died on Dec. 17, 1990. George Ortell died in July 2005 a few weeks before his 100th birthday. Two of her siblings, Louis A. and Mary Bonelli Cordingly, reside in Troy. Her brother Peter, who combined a career at RCA Victor Records with a Marketing position at British Airways in New York, is now retired and maintains a website on Olivia’s life and career from his residence in Jersey City. I am grateful to Peter for his assistance in contributing information for this article. Additional information on Olivia Bonelli, including photographs and reviews are available

www.oliviabonelli.com

. A new short glimpse of Olivia which includes excerpts from some of her operatic performances is available at

youtube.com/watch?v=j03CxZvBdcc

. What a glorious voice. Mike Esposito is a long time resident of Troy’s Little Italy neighborhood. “Troy Treasures” is a project of the Troy Rehabilitation and Improvement Program (TRIP), Inc.

case.old_text: Lidice (also known as The Butcher of Prague and Fall of the Innocent in the UK) is a 2011 Czech drama film produced by Adam Dvořák from a screenplay by Zdeněk Mahler. It was initially directed by Alice Nellis, but after she contracted Lyme disease (borreliosis), Petr Nikolaev took over. It tells a story involving the Nazi massacre at—and destruction of—the Czech village of Lidice. It was released in June 2011. The film is streaming on Amazon Prime under the title Fall of the Innocent (US, 15 April 2018).
